Smt.Shantubai And 04 Ors. vs Chandra Prakash And 02 Ors. on
4 September, 2025
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 4 th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 1023 of 2011
 Smt.Shantubai And 04 Ors.

And Others
 Versus
 Chandra Prakash And 02 Ors.

And Others
 Appearance:

Shri Manish Jain, learned counsel for the appellant
 Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the respo
 Order

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 25.02.2011 passed in claim case No.10/2010 challenging the quantum of compensation as well as issue of liability inasmuch as insurance company has been exonerated from the liability of compensation for absence of valid permit.

2. The short facts of the case are that on 30.06.2009, the deceased Deepsingh as well as one Jangliya were going in a Pick-up, when they reached near village-Junapaani, Umarkot Faate at Indore-Ahemdabad Highway road area, truck No.MP09-KD-9755 came which was insured with respondent No.3/insurance company and was being driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner.
The said truck rammed into the pick-up van in which the deceased Deepsingh was sitting because of which he sustained grievous injuries and died due to the said injuries.
2 MA-1023-2011 3. The claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Deepsing.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,23,000/- to the appellants/claimants.

However, while doing so the insurance company was exonerated from liability of payment of compensation on the ground that at the time of accident valid permit was not there with the offending vehicle.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants, at the outset, has pointed out that in the connected matter i.e.
in the claim petition filed by the other claimants arising out of the same accident, the claims tribunal has considered the claim in claim case No.137/2009 and in the said claim petition, award dated 27.06.2012 was passed in which the insurance company was held liable and it was also found that valid permit was available with the offending insured vehicle.

It was pointed out that the award was challenged by the claimant by filing MA No.1980/2012 in which enhancement was done by the Smt.Shantubai And 04 Ors. vs Chandra Prakash And 02 Ors. on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151290559/
1 coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 18.12.2012 again directing the respondent/insurance company to make payment of the enhanced amount.

entities.text: Smt.Shantubai And 04 Ors. vs Chandra Prakash And 02 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He thus submits that the exoneration of insurance company was not correct.
He further points out that he has even filed the copy of the permit along with his application under Order 41 Rule 27 (I.A. No.1961/2025).
Based on such submissions, the learned counsel for the appellant submits that insurance company should be made liable to pay the amount of compensation.

5. As regards the issue of income, the submission of the learned counsel is that although it was claimed before the claims tribunal that the deceased 3 MA-1023-2011 was earning Rs.200/- per day as such his earning was Rs.6000/- per month but, the claims tribunal has considered the income on notional basis at Rs.100/- per day, thus, the ultimate quantification of compensation for loss of dependency is very low.

He further submits that there are five claimants who are wife and children of the deceased, however, the claims tribunal has awarded amount of Rs.1000/- each to all five claimants for loss of consortium which is not in accordance with law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16) SCC 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the same count, he points out that the amount for funeral expenses including transportation of the dead body was awarded as Rs.6000/- which is also very less.

He also points out that looking to the number of dependents as five, the deduction made by the claims tribunal at 1/3rd is not correct in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104 a n d National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16) SCC 680, which should have been 1/4th.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also pointed out that multiplier of 13 has been applied whereas looking to the age bracket of the deceased between 40-45, multiplier of 14 should have been allowed.
Thus, he prays for enhancement of the compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company points out that the claimants failed to prove the income of the appellant as Rs.200/- per day.
There was complete absence of any material.
It was stated in the claim petition that the deceased used to go to Gujrat for earning his wages but there 4 MA-1023-2011 is no evidence in this behalf.
As such the claims tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.100/- per day.

As regards the liability of the insurance company, learned counsel does not dispute the fact that the insured vehicle was having permit at the time of accident as per the application filed under Order 41 Rule 27.
He is also not in position to dispute in passing of the award in connected case in miscellaneous appeal for the same accident in which insurance company was held liable.
However, he points out that only a meager amount of Rs.34000/- was involved in the said award, hence, the same was not challenged.

7. In addition to the above submissions, learned counsel for the insurance company also points out that in case this Court enhances the compensation and holds the insurance company liable for payment of compensation then also looking to the lethargy on the part of the appellant they are not entitled for payment of interest and they are entitled only for amount of compensation.

He points out that originally, the appeal was filed in the year 2011, notices were issued in the appeal only in the year 2014-15 and after 2014-15, the respondents/driver and owner were not served, for them the process fees was paid by the appellants only in the year of 2024.
As such, it is lethargy of the appellants due to which the appeal remained pending before this Court.

Hence, for this period, the Smt.Shantubai And 04 Ors. vs Chandra Prakash And 02 Ors. on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151290559/
2 insurance company should not be made liable to pay interest, in case, the company is held liable for payment of compensation.

sentences.text:
8. In rejoinder submission, learned counsel for the appellants points out that mere pendency of the appeal would not justify exclusion of the period 5 MA-1023-2011 for counting of interest on the award of compensation and for this submission, he placed reliance upon the judgment delivered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of T.C. John Vs. V.J. Antony, 2025 ACJ 24.
9.

entities.text: T.C. John Vs. V.J. Antony, 2025 ACJ 24
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

10. As regards the liability of the insurance company, it has undisputedly come on record that in the claim case No.137/2009 which was related to the same accident, the same insured vehicle and the same insurance company, the claims tribunal held the insurance company liable for payment of compensation.

Apart from this, permit has now been brought on record along with I.A.
No.1961/2025 which shows that the permit for the period covering the date of accident was very much there, which has now been verified by the insurance company also.
As such, this Court is of the considered view that for the reason of valid permit, the insurance company is liable for payment of compensation to the claimants in the present case also.

11. As regards the income, learned counsel while pointing out that the claim of Rs.200/- per day was made by the claimant has merely relied on the statement made by the claimant except this there was nothing before the claims tribunal to prove this claim.

However, on perusal of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority it is found that at the relevant time, the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer was Rs.3520/- as such the same is taken as income of the deceased Deep Singh.

12. So far as the amount of consortium is concerned, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16)
680, the amount is 6 MA-1023-2011 revised to Rs.40,000/- each to all five claimants totaling to Rs.2,00,000/- and for funeral expenses the amount is modified to Rs.15,000/-.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 (16)
680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from this, it is indisputable that there are five claimants of the deceased as such the deduction should have been made at 1/4th instead of 1/3rd, hence, the deduction for personal expenses is hereby changed to 1/4th and looking to the age of the deceased in the bracket of 40-45 years, the multiplier of 14 is applied.
In addition to it, 25% addition is made in the income of the deceased for future prospects.

While applying the above factors, the amount of compensation for loss of dependency comes to Rs.5,54,400/- and after including the amount of Rs.15000/- for loss of estate and adding the amount awarded in other heads, the total compensation now comes to Rs.7,84,400/-.
As such, now the original amount of compensation is Rs.3,23,000/- and enhanced amount of compensation is Rs.4,61,400/- over and above the original amount.

As the appellants have not been paid any thing,
the entire amount of Rs.7,84,400/- has to be paid to the appellants by the insurance company.

13. As regards the issue of interest, it is seen from the proceedings of the present appeal that after filing the present appeal in the year 2011, up to the month of July, 2014, learned counsel for the appellant continued to pray for time to pay the court fees and only on 25 July, 2014 court fees was paid.

As such it is hereby held that from the date of the application upto the date of actual payment Smt.Shantubai And 04 Ors. vs Chandra Prakash And 02 Ors. on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151290559/
3 of original amount of compensation at Rs.3,23,000/-, the appellants shall be entitled for amount of interest as originally directed by the claims tribunal and for enhanced amount of compensation of 7 MA-1023-2011 Rs.4,61,400/- the appellant shall be entitled for award of interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of the filing claim petition upto 18.04.2011 and then from 25.07.2014 till the actual amount is paid.
14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.
